correctness.rationale: Mazzolo arXiv:2609.22527, Eq. (116), supplies the exact finite-reactivity drifted mean time. For \(p=vL/(2D)>0\) and \(b=kL/(2D)>0\), the substitution \(u=\sqrt{p^2+rL^2/D}-p\) is strictly increasing in \(r\). Expanding the analytic numerator into positive Taylor coefficients makes the derivative numerator divided by \(u^2\) strictly increasing from negative infinity to positive infinity, establishing exactly one optimum for both drifts. At the inward optimum the outward derivative numerator equals \((1-e^{2p})d'(u)<0\), establishing strict global rate ordering. The log-stationarity expansion as \(p\) tends to infinity gives \(u_+=1-1/(2p)+O(p^{-2})\), \(u_-=1-(1/2+b/e)/p+O(p^{-2})\), and hence the nonzero dimensional gap \(k/(eL)\). CHECK.py passes 590 numerical and coefficient tests, supplemental only. Boundaries \(k=\infty\), \(v=0\) and non-Poisson clocks are excluded.

value.rationale: The source motivates optimal restart for physical constant drift and finite sink reactivity, where the inward optimum is numerically nonmonotone. Establishing an exact all-speed ordering under bias reversal resolves a global robustness question that cannot be concluded from the source local expansion or plot. The limit \(k/(eL)\) captures a finite, diffusivity-independent reactivity fingerprint invisible at leading rate \(v/L\) and explains the danger of taking perfect absorption before strong drift. This is a natural asymptotic classification of the entire model, not an arbitrary parameter slice; no independent application or experimental estimation guarantee is asserted.
